```{r filtering-setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(digits = 3)
```

Preprocessing steps describe changes to the data stored in a recipe. Adding a
step does not execute it: `prep()` applies preprocessing in the configured
order, before running differential-abundance methods. A recipe without a
statistical model is valid for preprocessing alone.

The examples below use the included data and run only preprocessing, not
statistical models. The thresholds illustrate the API; they are not universal
recommendations for microbiome studies.

## Inspect overall and grouped QC

```{r filtering-qc-before}
library(dar)
data("metaHIV_phy", package = "dar")

rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy)
recipe_qc(rec)
recipe_qc(rec, group_by = "RiskGroup2")
```

`recipe_qc()` summarizes the stored abundance matrix independently of any
model. It reports sample counts, sparsity, taxa detected in zero, one or two
samples, and library-size and count summaries. Singleton and doubleton metrics
refer to the number of samples with a detection, not to a taxon's total read
count. The `n` column counts matrix entries, not biological replicates.

With `group_by`, the overall row is followed by one row per observed metadata
group. The overall row has missing `group_by` and `group` identifiers; it is not
a group called `"all"`. Grouping is explicit and is not inferred from the
statistical target.

Use these summaries to inspect depth or sparsity differences between groups.
They do not establish the absence of confounding or that a particular filter
will improve statistical accuracy.

## Define and apply a shared preprocessing sequence

Here we first retain Bacteria and Archaea, then keep taxa observed in more than
3% of samples. These operations act on the stored features; selecting a rank
later with `add_model()` determines the taxonomic analysis view used by the DA
methods.

```{r filtering-shared-steps}
filtered_rec <- rec |>
  step_subset_taxa(
    tax_level = "Kingdom", taxa = c("Bacteria", "Archaea")
  ) |>
  step_filter_by_prevalence(threshold = 0.03)

filtered <- prep(filtered_rec, parallel = FALSE)
```

`step_subset_taxa()` matches annotations at the specified rank. The prevalence
filter then uses all samples in the recipe, not one threshold calculated
separately within each QC group. Preprocessing preserves the original input
object; the prepared recipe contains the filtered data.

Compare the stored data before and after preprocessing:

```{r filtering-qc-after}
data.frame(
  stage = c("before", "after"),
  n_taxa = c(nrow(dar::otu_table(rec)), nrow(dar::otu_table(filtered)))
)
recipe_qc(filtered)
recipe_qc(filtered, group_by = "RiskGroup2")
```

Order matters. An abundance threshold expressed relative to all reads uses the
total remaining at that point in the sequence. Resampling before a prevalence
filter can change which taxa pass it. Specify the intended order explicitly,
and remember that engines may also apply their own internal filters. A shared
input does not make every engine's tested-feature set or assumptions identical.

## Choose a filtering predicate

The convenience wrappers apply across-sample criteria to each stored taxon:

| Step | Criterion for retaining a taxon |
|:--|:--|
| `step_filter_by_prevalence(threshold)` | Proportion of samples with nonzero abundance is strictly greater than the threshold. |
| `step_filter_by_abundance(threshold)` | Its total abundance is strictly greater than the threshold times the total abundance of the current table. |
| `step_filter_by_variance(threshold)` | Its across-sample variance is strictly greater than the threshold, on the stored abundance scale. |
| `step_filter_by_rarity(threshold)` | Proportion of samples with nonzero abundance is strictly below the threshold. |

`step_filter_by_rarity()` selects rare taxa; it does not remove rare taxa.
Use `step_filter_by_prevalence()` for that purpose. The variance threshold is
not a proportion and depends on the abundance units.

For a custom rule, `step_filter_taxa()` accepts a function with exactly one
argument named `x` and no default. This example includes taxa exactly on the 3%
boundary, unlike the strict prevalence wrapper above.

```{r filtering-custom-predicate}
custom_rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  step_filter_taxa(.f = function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 0.03 * length(x))
```

The same predicate may be supplied as a character string:

```{r filtering-custom-string}
custom_string_rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  step_filter_taxa(.f = "function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 0.03 * length(x)")
```

Both forms return a recipe, not filtered data or a logical vector. The
predicate must return one logical value when applied to each abundance vector
during `prep()`; the wrapper has no `prune` argument.

To keep recipes safely serializable, the predicate body must be a single
expression. Braces, assignments, external variables, namespace-qualified calls,
user-defined helpers and lists of functions are not supported, even in local R
use. Write thresholds as literal numbers. Accepted expressions include
arithmetic, comparisons, logical operators and approved summaries such as
`sum`, `mean`, `median`, `var` and `sd`; see `?step_filter_taxa` for the complete
syntax and supported `na.rm` arguments. The restrictions are checked when the
step is added, not only on export.

## Rarefaction is optional

The workflow above does not rarefy. `step_rarefaction()` is available when an
explicitly chosen analysis calls for shared equal-depth resampling:

```{r filtering-rarefaction, eval = FALSE}
rarefied_rec <- recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  step_rarefaction()
rarefied <- prep(rarefied_rec, parallel = FALSE)
```

This is not a general recommendation to normalize DA inputs by rarefaction.
Subsampling discards observations and changes the data supplied to downstream
methods. Select preprocessing in the context of the scientific question and
the methods' assumptions; equal library sizes do not guarantee valid inference.
`rarefaction_help()` describes the cautions in more detail.

Some DA steps also accept `rarefy = TRUE` to resample only for that step, rather
than altering the shared preprocessing data. For those configured DA steps,
the informational note about rarefaction's controversy appears during `prep()`,
not when the step is added. A shared `step_rarefaction()` and a method-specific
`rarefy` option are different configurations; do not combine them unless repeat
resampling is intentional.

For selecting a central statistical model after defining preprocessing, see
[Statistical models and contrasts](statistical_models.html).
